articles.title: Rattlesnake Blood Hides a Powerful Antivenom—and Scientists Cracked It
articles.summary: Rattlesnakes are immune to their own venom. Scientists discovered that mixing certain proteins from their blood creates an antivenom 10 times stronger than the current one. This could save thousands of lives from deadly snakebites.

articles.title: Dancing Swifties Shook the Ground—and Scientists Are Listening
articles.summary: A Taylor Swift concert in 2023 made the ground vibrate like a minor earthquake. Scientists study these human-made seismic waves to build safer buildings and understand crowd movements. Even COVID lockdowns caused 'seismic quiet.'

articles.title: When a $264 Million Spacecraft Crashed: The Genesis Mission's Close Call
articles.summary: In 2004, NASA's Genesis spacecraft crashed in Utah because its parachute failed—a simple design flaw. The solar wind samples shattered, but scientists salvaged some. It was NASA's first sample-return mission since Apollo 17.
